Details: Category: Speed Duration: 2 Hours Date: 17th October 2026 Time: 12:00 PM Venue: Guru Tegh Bahadur Institute of Technology Mode: Offline Team Size: 3–5 participants No. of rounds: 2 attempts per team (3 laps per attempt; best valid attempt considered) Eligibility Criteria: Open to all students. Inter-college participants allowed. Pre-requisites: Competition-ready wireless-controlled rover complying with the specifications below: Maximum weight: 2 kg Maximum dimensions: 8 × 8 × 8 inches Maximum voltage: 48V DC Control: Wireless only — Wi-Fi, BLE, RF, LoRa, nRF24L01, or commercial RC systems Operator: Single operator per run Wired control: Not permitted Event Flow: One rover will be allowed on the track at a time. Missing a checkpoint will result in lap invalidation or a +20 second penalty , as determined by the organisers. raw.details:
Overdrive is a high-speed wireless rover racing challenge that tests speed, precision, control, and driving skills. Teams compete to complete a Melbourne F1-style track featuring ramps, rollers, gravel pits, and airborne sections in the shortest possible time. With 3 laps per attempt and 2 attempts per team, racers must balance aggressive driving with precision while avoiding penalties. The fastest valid run conquers the track.

"Accelerate. Control. Conquer."

Details:

  • Category: Speed
  • Duration: 2 Hours
  • Date: 17th October 2026
  • Time: 12:00 PM
  • Venue: Guru Tegh Bahadur Institute of Technology
  • Mode: Offline
  • Team Size: 3–5 participants
  • No. of rounds: 2 attempts per team (3 laps per attempt; best valid attempt considered)

Eligibility Criteria:

  • Open to all students.
  • Inter-college participants allowed.

Pre-requisites:

Competition-ready wireless-controlled rover complying with the specifications below:

  • Maximum weight: 2 kg
  • Maximum dimensions: 8 × 8 × 8 inches
  • Maximum voltage: 48V DC
  • Control: Wireless only — Wi-Fi, BLE, RF, LoRa, nRF24L01, or commercial RC systems
  • Operator: Single operator per run
  • Wired control: Not permitted

Event Flow:

  • One rover will be allowed on the track at a time.
  • Each team gets 2 attempts, with 3 laps per attempt.
  • Each attempt has a maximum time limit of 5 minutes.
  • Checkpoint detection will be performed using a front-mounted white LED and LDR-based checkpoint system.
  • The Final Time = Race Time + Penalty Time.
  • The team with the lowest valid Final Time will rank highest.
  • Tie-breaker: lower penalty time will be considered first; if still tied, the better time from the team's other attempt will be considered.
  • Failure to complete all 3 laps within the time limit will result in DNF.

Rules & Regulations:

  • The rover must comply with the specified 2 kg weight, 8-inch maximum dimensions, and 48V DC maximum voltage limits.
  • Only wireless control is permitted. Wired control of the rover is strictly prohibited.
  • Each rover must have a front-mounted white LED that remains visible to the checkpoint detection system throughout the run.
  • Only one operator is permitted to control the rover during an attempt.
  • Weapons, projectiles, explosives, pyrotechnics, flammable substances, high-pressure systems, or any mechanism designed to damage another rover or person are strictly prohibited.
  • Any form of jamming or intentional signal interference with another team's rover is prohibited.
  • Knocking a boundary or obstacle will incur a +3 second penalty.
  • An off-track excursion will incur a +5 second penalty.
  • A manual reset will incur a +10 second penalty.
  • Missing a checkpoint will result in lap invalidation or a +20 second penalty, as determined by the organisers.
  • Unsafe or reckless driving may result in a warning and, if repeated or severe, disqualification.
  • A rover that fails to complete all 3 laps within the 5-minute limit will be marked DNF.
